# Establishment log — popol-vuh-015 (image 0047 from line 43, 0048, 0049, and 0050 to line 31)

Read 2026-11-26 by the routine's own model from source/pages/i0047 (l.43–46, after `… Hunahpu Coy xqui zuah.`),
all of i0048 and i0049, and i0050 lines 1–31, in strips of about six lines at 0.7–0.9×, with 1.1–2.2× crops of
every doubtful word, checked word by word against Brasseur 1861 (OCR lines 23771–23775, 23838–23900, 23930–23960,
24047–24180). Pillow was taken into a scratch venv (the system PIL is broken in this container).

Start: `Catepuch xe bixanic, xe zuanic, xe cohomanic …` (0047 l.43, Ximénez's indented paragraph). End:
`… Xa hun acab xqui bano.` (0050 l.30–31). **The part ends at the episode joint** after the animals restore the
field in one night; 0050 l.31 continues `Cate chicut xqui tiquiba chic abixic …` (the second clearing and the night
watch), where popol-vuh-016 should begin. Image 0051 was not needed.

parts.json: popol-vuh-016 set to images 0050–0053 (first_image 50, last_image 53, cite `LoC images 0050–0053`;
it was 0054–0056, which would have left 0051–0053 unread); plan.md row updated. 017 untouched.

Content: the twins play and sing, the grandmother sits with them; the tune Hunahpu Coy; Hunbaꜩ and Hunchouen come
dancing; the grandmother sees their ugly faces and laughs, and they run off; four tries — at the second she laughs
at their bellies, tails and chests; at the third at their red eyes and grimaces on the roof; at the fourth they
do not come; the twins console her ("we are here, your grandchildren"); the elder brothers were invoked by the
flautists and singers, painters and carvers of old, and became monkeys for their pride and their mistreatment of
their younger brothers. New indented paragraph (0049 l.14): the twins begin their work, the field; axe and hoe;
the grandmother to bring food at noon; the hoe clears and the axe fells by itself; the dove Xmucur set on a stump
to coo when she comes; they dirty their hands and heads with earth and chips; they come home "tired"; next day the
field has grown back, and it was all the animals, large and small, in one night.

## Folios
Counting as 004–014 did (0047 = 19r): 0048 = 19v, 0049 = 20r, 0050 = 20v → `fols. 19r–20v`. The crops of 0048 and
0050 carry `19` and `20` at the top left (the folio doubt in QUESTIONS.md, 2026-11-24, again); the earlier count is
kept.

## Paragraphs
Ximénez indents 0047 l.43 (`Catepuch xe bixanic`) and 0049 l.14 (`Ta xqui tiquiba chicut qui banoh`); the other
paragraphs are cut at speech turns and episode joints, as 011–014 did.

## Letter rule used (002–014's rules, unchanged)
- g-shaped → ꜭ where Brasseur has q: `ri catit cuꜭ` (0047 l.46, MS `cug`), `vchi qui ꜭux` (0048 l.21), `qui ꜭux`
  (0049 l.7), `oh ꜭolic` ×2 (MS `ohgolic`; B. qolic), `ruꜭ` ×4 (MS `rug`); gh → ꜭh: `xeꜭha`, `xꜭha`, `queꜭha`,
  `que vꜭhaxic`.
- **g-shaped where Brasseur has g (= ꜫ)**: `ꜫatoh cheenel` (0050 l.13, MS `gatoh`; B. gatoh). The letter has no u
  after it, so the hand is ambiguous between the g-shape (ꜭ) and the q-shape (ꜫ); Brasseur decided (ꜫ). Modern
  q'atoj 'cut' agrees.
- **`xe ꜭobic`** (0048 l.46, MS `xegobic`, g-shaped; B. `x-e cobie`, plain c). Brasseur does not help; printed by
  the shape rule. Meaning uncertain — drafter to mark it.
- q-shaped + u where Brasseur has g → ꜫ, u dropped: `qui hoꜫih` (0048 l.32–33, MS `hoquih`; B. hogih), `e
  ramaꜫelal` (0049 l.10, MS `ramaquelal`; B. r'amagelal), `qui ꜫexel` (0049 l.19, MS `quexel`; house vꜫexel),
  `na ꜫih` (0049 l.25, MS `quih`; B. gih), `cat oꜫic` (0049 l.47, MS `catoquic`; B. c'at ogic), `chu caꜫih`
  (0050 l.21, MS `chucaquih`; B. chaka gih).
- tresillo (3/ε-shaped) → ꜫ: **`caꜫruxruh`** (0048 l.30; B. ca-kruxruh, k), **`ꜫaꜫchacachoh`** (0049 l.36, both
  letters ε-shaped; B. cakchacachoh, k — as 014's ꜫaꜫvachibal), `aꜫ` (0050 l.29, 'pig/peccary'; B. ak), `qui ꜫab`
  (0050 l.20; B. gab).
- Plain c kept where the MS has plain c and Brasseur g/q (unmarked ejectives stay unmarked): `calabil` (B. galabil),
  `chu cab rib` (0049 l.34; B. gab), `pu cab` (0050 l.9; B. gab), `chi catoh che` (0049 l.36; B. gatoh), `xe
  coheic` (0049 l.12; B. qoheic — 014 had g-shaped ꜭoheic), `co cochoch` (B. qo c'ochoch), `xqui yoc ri qui chac`
  (B. yog, chag), `xaloc` ×4 (B. xalog), `choc` (0050 l.5; B. ch'og), **`xa hun acab`** (0050 l.30, clearly plain c
  at 2×; B. agab; the house word is aꜫab where the MS writes the tresillo).
- tz ligature → ꜩ: `iꜩel`, `vꜩe` ×4, `xꜩeenic`, `xꜩeen`, `ꜩeebal`, `chu ꜩeeh`, `vꜩebal`, `Hunbaꜩ`, `caꜩ`, `ꜩac`,
  `muꜩumac`, `quiꜩih`, `ꜩaꜩ`, `chu ꜩiloh`, `coꜩic`, `Vꜩ bala` ×2; tz' → ꜯ: `ꜯiquin` ×2 (the house word, as 014).
- z (ʒ-shaped) kept: `piz` (0050 l.7; B. piz), `Quiz` (0050 l.22; B. qiz), `ziz`.

## Abbreviations expanded
- `catit`, `atit` throughout (MS `cah̃t`, `ah̃t`), as 012–014.
- **`oh iviy`** ×2 (0048 l.44, 0049 l.19; MS `ivy` with a mark above) and **`ix viy`** (0049 l.27; MS `ixvy` with
  the same mark); B. y'viy, yx viy. The mark is read as an abbreviation of the i of viy.
- `caam` (0049 l.35, MS `caã`; B. caam).
- `chuti` (0050 l.29, MS `chuh̃`; B. chüti).

## Against Brasseur — the image followed
- `ta vcamic ri qui zu` (B. u qamic), `xu cui` (0048 l.5, MS `xucui`; B. x-u cuy), `chu cuiu ca vꜩe` (0048 l.28,
  MS `chucuiuca`; B. ch'u cuyu ca) — but `qui chi cuyu iꜩe` (0048 l.11, y clear).
- `pa tac huiub` (0048 l.23; B. huyub), `iaol ca va`, `iaoc qui va` (B. yaol, yaoc), `iacatahinac` (B. vacatahinak).
- `pu holom` (0050 l.12, MS `puholom`; B. u holom), `quehe viri` (0050 l.13, MS `queheuiri`, Ximénez's r v-shaped;
  B. З viri), `que banou ri` (0050 l.26, joined; B. que bano u ri).
- `chutuquel` (0049 l.32, plain t; B. ch'utuquel).
- `tum` (0049 l.39) and `tum` (0050 l.24, written with only two minims, `tun`; B. tam both) — printed tum both.
- `coh` (0050 l.28, plain c; the animal ꜭoh of 002 was g-shaped there).

## Doubtful readings — for the drafter's notes
- **`Eia, catit!`** (0048 l.7, MS `eia cahic`: the last word lacks its final stroke; read catit; B. Eya! k'atit).
- **`Catiha china`** (0048 l.11–12, MS `cathha / china`, the t written like h; B. ca üha chi na).
- **`xchi ca bano`** (0048 l.24): the first letter is q-shaped; read x (B. `chi ka bano`, no x).
- **`Xavi cu ꜫuz`** (0048 l.15–16, MS `xa | vi ququz`: two q/g-shaped letters, each followed by u; B. `xavi eu guz`
  = cu ꜫuz): first read c (B.), second ꜫ (B. g). The weakest reading in the part.
- **`ca qui tacchih`** (0048 l.17, MS `tac chih`, two words on the page; B. takchyih) — joined.
- **`chi chitila he puch`** (0048 l.20, MS `chichihta he`: tall strokes after chichi; B. chi chitila he) —
  Brasseur's reading taken.
- **`macama`** (0048 l.32): an ink blot on the second a; B. makamo.
- **`chi qui yuc puch cacan`** (0050 l.19, MS `chiquaʒiuc` or similar: a q-shape, a, a ʒ-like y, a u written like
  in; B. `chi qui yug puch c akan`) — printed after Brasseur's word with the MS's plain final c.
- **`Chi qui piz la qui vi`** (0050 l.7–8, `piz` at line end, `la` at the start of the next; B. piz la) — kept
  apart as Brasseur.
- `quicah` (0049 l.21, MS `quicah`; B. qu'icah = qui icah) printed joined, the reader tokenizes it whole.
- `xaqui xqui chiquiba` (0049 l.28–29; B. xaki).
- `pa cabix` (0050 l.22; B. pa c'abix = ca abix 'our field'), joined as written.
- `cocochoch` → `co cochoch` (0049 l.10–11, MS `cocho-|ch` with a doubled c at the join).
